# SOP-P2-L3-02 Product changeover - Machining line
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, EQ-P2-L3-IH03  
Related documents: SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-03, SOP-P2-L3-05

1. Purpose and scope
1.1. Purpose: Define the standard operating procedure for product changeover on the machining line P2-L3 to ensure safe transition, preserve equipment integrity, and maintain part quality. This SOP applies to operations performed on the equipment listed above during changeover sequences that involve radial ring rolling, heat treatment staging, and induction billet heating.
1.2. Scope: Covers preconditions, required PPE, stepwise changeover tasks, verification checks, examples of common changeover scenarios, records to keep, and final sign-off.

2. Background and rationale
2.1. Background: Changeovers create transient states where machine settings, tooling, and lubricant regimes are adjusted. Controlled procedures reduce the risk of mechanical damage, contamination, and out-of-spec parts. This SOP consolidates best practices for this line and ties into SB-1036 for lubrication management and SOP-P2-L3-03 and SOP-P2-L3-05 for downstream process handling and verification.
2.2. Rationale: Specified lubricant selection and billet temperature targets are critical control points. Using the designated lubricant for the radial ring rolling mill prevents premature wear and surface defects. Maintaining target billet temperature at the induction heater reduces microstructural deviation and machining issues.

3. Preconditions (must be confirmed before initiating changeover)
3.1. Production control has released the changeover order and provided part program identifiers.
3.2. All operators assigned to the changeover have read and understand this SOP, SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-03, and SOP-P2-L3-05.
3.3. Equipment EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03 are on their respective maintenance logs and show no outstanding critical maintenance flags.
3.4. All required PPE is available for each operator performing tasks.
3.5. The lubricant part number for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is CFW-LUB-225.
3.6. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C.

4. PPE (minimum)
4.1. Cut-resistant gloves suitable for handling tooling and hot parts.
4.2. Heat-resistant face shield and apron for tasks involving heated billets.
4.3. Safety shoes with metatarsal protection.
4.4. Hearing protection as required by plant policy.
4.5. Safety glasses with side protection.
Note: Consult plant safety rules for any additional PPE based on job hazard analysis.

5. Step-by-step changeover procedure
5.1. Initial isolation and lockout
5.1.1. Notify downstream and upstream work centers of impending changeover.
5.1.2. Place the equipment in a safe state following lockout-tagout procedures. Verify isolation according to plant LOTO protocol.
5.2. Remove and catalog previous tooling and fixtures
5.2.1. Drain or capture any residual fluids from tooling interfaces per SB-1036 guidance.
5.2.2. Label removed tooling and store in designated locations to prevent cross-contamination.
5.3. Inspect and replenish lubrication
5.3.1. Verify current lubricant inventory and selector valve positions for EQ-P2-L3-RR01.
5.3.2. Install lubricant CFW-LUB-225 to the radial ring rolling mill reservoir following SB-1036 storage and handling instructions.
5.3.3. Record the lubricant lot and dispenser ID on the changeover log.
Rationale: Ensures compatibility with bearing and slide materials; prevents unexpected material transfer and surface defects.
5.4. Set up new tooling and gross alignment
5.4.1. Fit new tooling per fixture diagram and torque to clamping fixtures using calibrated tools (see tooling vendor documentation).
5.4.2. Perform gross alignment using mechanical references; do not energize drives until electrical checks are complete.
5.5. Start-up of heating systems and temperature verification
5.5.1. Bring EQ-P2-L3-IH03 to operational state per manufacturer startup checklist.
5.5.2. Configure the induction heater control to reach the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C. Allow stabilization per control system guidance.
Rationale: Correct billet temperature reduces machining stress and ensures metallurgical targets are met.
5.6. Dry-run and trial pieces
5.6.1. Run a dry-cycle without workpiece to verify interlocks, feed paths, and coolant flows.
5.6.2. Process a trial billet through the line, observe for mechanical contact, chatter, unusual noise, or surface anomalies.
5.6.3. Inspect trial parts per incoming inspection criteria in SOP-P2-L3-03.
5.7. Adjustments and confirmation
5.7.1. If defects are detected, make incremental adjustments to tool offsets and clamping; reprocess trial parts until acceptable.
5.7.2. Confirm machine parameters and control setpoints are logged and retained in the changeover record.
5.8. Resume production
5.8.1. Upon acceptance of trial parts, release the line for production with clear batch identifiers.
5.8.2. Communicate the lubricant lot and billet temperature confirmation to quality and downstream teams.

6. Examples and common scenarios
6.1. Example: Tool interference detected during trial. Action: Stop machine, check fixture datum, re-seat tooling, verify CFW-LUB-225 application to sliding surfaces, re-run trial.
6.2. Example: Surface scale observed on first machined face. Action: Verify EQ-P2-L3-IH03 reached and stabilized at the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C and review heater control logs; consult SOP-P2-L3-05 for downstream scale mitigation.

7. Records to keep
7.1. Changeover log with:
7.1.1. Operator names and signatures.
7.1.2. Lubricant used with lot/dispense ID (must record CFW-LUB-225 when used).
7.1.3. Trial part inspection results and disposition.
7.1.4. Heater control confirmation indicating attainment of the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C.
7.2. Tooling inventory sheet showing removed and installed tooling identifiers.
7.3. Deviations and nonconformance reports linked to SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-03, or SOP-P2-L3-05 as applicable.

8. Sign-off
8.1. Changeover completed by: __________________________ (print name, operator)
8.2. Verified by: __________________________ (print name, shift lead)
8.3. Quality sign-off: __________________________ (print name, QA)
8.4. Maintenance confirmation (if lubrication or mechanical work performed): __________________________ (print name, maintenance)
8.5. Notes: Attach all records listed in section 7 and reference SB-1036, SOP-P2-L3-03, SOP-P2-L3-05 as applicable for follow-up actions.

Revision control: Maintain this document in the document control system and reference SB-1036 for lubrication procedures; use SOP-P2-L3-03 and SOP-P2-L3-05 for downstream inspection and handling requirements.
